decisive_items: Figure 1. Title: Recurrent Melanoma Lesions on the Left Posterior Auricular Scalp Before and After T-VEC Therapy
Figure 2. Title: Histopathologic Findings of T-VEC–Treated Melanoma Lesions
complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation; MART-1 immunostain confirms complete tumor regression
response.rationale: R2 directly names the T-VEC treatment context and matches the histopathologic finding of complete tumor regression with neutrophil-rich inflammation. R3 captures regression but lacks the specific T-VEC diagnosis; R5/R6 are contradicted by the absence of viable melanoma on MART-1 and SOX-10 staining.

rejected.why: The inflammatory infiltrate is treatment-related regression, not inflammatory melanoma; no melanoma cells are identified.
Describes tumor regression but is less specific than T-VEC-treated melanoma and omits the T-VEC figure evidence.
Immune-mediated reaction is a mechanism, not the specific diagnosis, and does not account for the T-VEC context.
Recurrent melanoma is contradicted by complete regression and MART-1 highlighting only normal basal melanocytes.
Too broad; viable melanoma is excluded by histology and immunostaining.
Drug-induced inflammation is a component of the response but not the overall diagnosis of T-VEC-treated melanoma.
